messages:
Maya: quick design review — trying to reconcile pool filtering with burst affordance. current mock stacks burst pill next to pool name and it reads like a tag, but behavior is different.
Ravi: agree. users think burst is a property of the pool, not an action. that mismatch trips a lot of folks during testing.
Sam: can we treat burst more like a control (toggle/override) rather than a tag? visually that would mean a button affordance instead of a pill.
Casey: +1. also the min/max slider is stealing visual weight from SLO knob. when both visible the eye goes to the big slider and misses SLO entirely.
Maya: proposal: compact pool rows, left-aligned pool selector, then a subtle burst action icon on the right edge that opens the burst overlay. keep burst pill only in the burst modal header.
Ravi: that keeps the row tidy. what about keyboard users? right now the pill isn't in tab order properly.
Sam: accessibility nit — if burst is an action, ensure it has role=button and aria-expanded when the overlay is open. example:

```html
<button class="burst-action" role="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="burst-popover">Burst</button>
``` 

Casey: love that. also microcopy: replace "Burst" -> "Burst (temporary capacity)" in the popover header and add a one-line hint: "Used for short spikes; not guaranteed for long-running jobs." small but helpful.
Maya: SLO slider needs a guardrail tooltip that explains tradeoffs. testers often slam SLO to the right expecting lower cost, but we want them to understand latency vs cost tradeoff.
Ravi: tooltip text suggestion: "Higher SLO (left) prioritizes latency, lower SLO (right) prioritizes cost savings. We may fall back to smaller model variants to save capacity." feels a bit wordy.
Sam: shorten: "Higher SLO = lower latency, higher cost. Lower SLO = cheaper, may use fallback models." keep it inline with the slider tick labels.
Casey: design question — when a pool can't burst (quota/exhausted), show disabled burst icon with tooltip + a CTA to request capacity. prefer inline link: "Request burst" opens support flow.
Maya: visual weight: make SLO knob 14px, slider track 2px, primary color for active thumb. move min/max numbers into a secondary, lighter row to reduce dominance.
Ravi: also add a visual mapping from burst size to expected latency improvement — maybe a subtle sparkline or tiny bars inside the burst modal.
Sam: tiny bars are good. ensure we label them for screen readers: aria-hidden for decorative bars, and provide textual summary like "Estimated latency improvement: 10–30%."
Casey: copy tweak: change confirmation for destructive autoscale changes from "Apply" to "Save capacity targets" — less vague.
Maya: last thing — mobile/tablet: pool selector collapses to single-line with chevron, and burst action should be reachable via swipe menu (or a 3-dot overflow). we tested and overflow felt natural.
Designbot: prototyping note recorded: updated figma screens with burst-as-action pattern + SLO tooltip variants. @Maya @Ravi please review before dev handoff :eyes:
Maya: will review end of day and post updated flows. tagging @Sam for a quick accessibility pass once updated.
